implementation_notes: Java 8 absorbed the pattern: a lambda that uses enclosing locals compiles to a class whose fields hold copies of those values, so `Function<Integer, Integer> add5 = y -> add(5, y);` is a partial application, and java.util.function supplies both the vocabulary types (Function, BiFunction, UnaryOperator) and the sequencing operators andThen/compose/identity. Method references bind a receiver the same way (store::get, this::handle). Before Java 8 the equivalent was an anonymous class implementing a single-method interface, and the low-level route remains MethodHandle.bindTo, which the JDK documents as an insertion transformation that prepends the receiver to a typed, directly executable reference - use it for reflective and framework plumbing, not for readable application code.
pitfalls: Lambdas capture effectively final values only, so a binding cannot be mutated afterwards; callers rebuild the specialisation instead, which is easy to miss inside a loop.
Generic functional interfaces box primitives: Function<Integer, Integer> boxes on every call - use the primitive specialisations (IntUnaryOperator, IntBinaryOperator) in hot paths.
Recomposing with andThen inside a loop allocates a new lambda per iteration; hoist the composed function like any other specialisation.
